newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X, Minorca to resume trading.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X, Minorca to resume trading.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Minorca Resources Inc shares will resume trading at 1500 EST/2000 GMT, the Toronto Stock Exchange said on Thursday.
The stocks have been halted since before the open on Wednesday. The TSE asked Bre-X for further information this morning and Bre-X issued a statement at 1358 EST/1858 GMT.

"Since Bre-X has provided the market with the current information known to the company concerning the confirmatory drilling conducted to date by Freeport-McMoRan (Copper & Gold Inc) and the immediate plans of both Freeport and Bre-X for further work on the property, it is appropriate to re-open trading," the TSE said in a statement.
Bre-X said that tests on the Busang gold site by partner Freeport-McMoRan have indicated "insignificant amounts of gold" and visual differences in gold particles from core holes.
Bre-X included the results of confirmatory drilling conducted to date by New Orleans-based Freeport-McMoRan.

The gold exploration company also expressed its concerns to the Toronto Stock Exchange regarding the resumption of trading in Bre-X shares before an independent audit of its Busang findings is complete.
The TSE said its task is to provide a continuous market in securities for investors.
"We understand that a gray market has developed in the U.S. to which only a limited group of investors has access, and the market is best served by a visible and accessible exchange," the TSE said.
It said waiting for the completion of the audit means it could take weeks or longer for definitive information to emerge.
"The exchange does not believe that it is appropriate to deprive shareholders and investors of a market for such a lengthy period of time," the TSE said.
